items.body: The fn-257 verifier pinned the export tip with `mapping[SOURCE] == checkpoint`. The fn-258 adaptation relaxes this to `mapping[SOURCE] in {checkpoint, None}`. When the source tip is projection-neutral (the actual case here: the ac60 row is zero), nothing bounds the checkpoint to the commit map. The remaining checks are one-directional: every retained mapped commit must be reachable from the checkpoint, and the checkpoint tree must equal the manifest. Concrete failing scenario: in an export clone run `git commit-tree a92db06^{tree} -p a92db06 -m injected` and pass that commit as `--checkpoint`. All 627 retained commits are reachable, the pruned ac60 frontier is still `{a92db06}` with an equal tree, the final tree equals the 1,189-file manifest, and the worktree checks pass. The verifier reports `pass` for a history containing an unmapped commit with arbitrary author, date and message. The README claims the zero row is accepted only "alongside ... independent neutrality/reachability checks", but reachability alone does not establish that the exported history consists of exactly the mapped commits. The negative controls (file corruption, missing map row, injected sibling parent) do not exercise this path. The committed evidence itself is sound because a92db06 is the mapped image of 192dd9ce (commit-map row 736), so this is a verifier gap rather than a bad artifact.
items.suggestion: After building `export_graph`, add `require(set(export_graph) == {new for new in mapping.values() if new}, "export-graph-bounded", ...)`, and when `mapping[SOURCE]` is None additionally require that the checkpoint is a member of the pruned source's computed retained frontier. Re-run verification and add a negative control for an unmapped tip commit.
